text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ جَعَلْنَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ حِجَابًۭا مَّسْتُورًۭا

baseline.text: Kur'an okuduğunda seninle ahirete inanmayanların arasına görünmez bir perde koyarız.

findings.text: Kur'an'ın okunması görünmez ayrılığı yoktan üretmez; ahirete güvenmeyenlerin karşılaşma anında işleyen ilişki uyumsuzluğunu görünür ve etkin hale getirir.

activation_trace.role: Literal reading and recitation supply the event that initiates the boundary.
Active production makes the boundary an effected condition rather than a pre-existing obstacle.
The middle interval locates the mechanism relationally between two parties.
Prevention of access gives the interval its operative force.
Covering applies to the barrier itself, making the cause of non-access covert.

changed_reading.after: Each recitation event actively configures an unseen access boundary: speech may be present while the reason it does not pass remains hidden.
changed_reading.before: The hearers simply fail to receive the recitation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The recitation event, the doubled relational interval at words 5-6, and the barrier-plus-modifier at words 11-12.
baseline_models.mechanism: Recitation initiates a divine making: the interval between reciter and resistant hearers is constituted as blocked access, while the blocker is itself covered from inspection.

activation_trace.role: Heart-settled assent supplies the denied receptive stance.
Deferral to a later time makes futurity the object of the denied assent.
Expanded distance converts temporal refusal into a present gap between parties.
Blocked access is the present effect attached to that deferred horizon.

changed_reading.after: A rejected future horizon structures present perception, turning deferred non-assent into immediate distance from recited speech.
changed_reading.before: Nonbelief in the Hereafter is only an audience label.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The audience is identified by negated assent at word 9 toward what is later at word 10, immediately before the barrier.
baseline_models.mechanism: Failure of heart-settled assent toward the deferred horizon is translated into present relational distance; the later is not merely a doctrine named but the temporal orientation that organizes current non-access.

activation_trace.role: Blocked access anchors the changed mechanism in the focus ayah.
Turning material through different states supplies repeated variation of presentation.
Recitation identifies the medium whose repeated presentation is being tested.
Recovery into awareness supplies the intended receptive outcome.
Growth supplies the positive feedback that magnifies the actual response.
Recoil and distancing specify the response that the feedback increases.

changed_reading.after: Recitation dynamically strengthens the very distancing it is capable of overcoming, so added exposure can thicken rather than remove the boundary.
changed_reading.before: The veil is a static screen encountered during recitation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding sequence makes recitation an amplifier with opposite possible outputs: varied presentation is directed toward recollection, yet in these hearers it produces additional recoil. The veil therefore describes an inverted reception process, not mere absence of exposure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies variation -> intended recollection -> increase -> recoil; I infer that the veil names this inverted reception loop, while a live alternative is a protective boundary independent of hearer reaction.
structural_cues: 17:41 orders varied presentation, a recollection-purpose clause, exclusive increase, and recoil immediately before the focus.

activation_trace.role: Prevention of access anchors the distinction between arrival and uptake.
The covered mechanism explains why audible contact need not reveal the obstruction.
Failed comprehension distinguishes semantic uptake from the presence of expression.
Protective concealment relocates one layer of the barrier inward.
The physical organ marks the auditory channel on which the next burden operates.
Auditory heaviness makes reception effortful without requiring total silence.
Repeated perception of sound proves that acoustic contact survives the barrier.

changed_reading.after: The audience can hear while semantic recognition and responsive access are screened by a distributed, unobserved filter.
changed_reading.before: The hidden veil prevents the audience from hearing the reciter.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus barrier is distributed across uptake rather than simple audibility: comprehension fails, inward material is covered, ears carry a burden, yet listening still occurs. Sound crosses; intelligible and responsive reception does not.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-comprehension, inward concealment, ear burden, and repeated listening; I infer a layered filter after acoustic arrival, with literal sensory impairment remaining a narrower alternative.
structural_cues: 17:44 denies comprehension, 17:46 places inward coverings and auditory weight, and 17:47 twice asserts listening.

activation_trace.role: A screening partition anchors the proposed interpretive rather than acoustic barrier.
Attributing an unreal description supplies the substitutive label placed over the speaker.
Diversion and deception provide the content of the hostile explanatory frame.
Actively presenting a comparison turns the label into a constructed model.
The formulated analogy is the cognitive object that displaces direct reception.
Loss of intended direction supplies the consequence of adopting the countermodel.
A traversable path supplies what the countermodel leaves unavailable.

changed_reading.after: The veil can operate as a replacement model generated after hearing, screening the recitation by redescribing its bearer.
changed_reading.before: The veil is an object standing between speech and hearers.

context_deltas.mechanism: After listening, the hearers replace the reciter with a hostile explanatory label and then circulate analogical models. Those models function as the veil's visible output: they interpret the speaker away and leave no traversable route to what is recited.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies listening -> labeling -> analogical construction -> path failure; I infer that the labels mediate the failure, while the live alternative is that slander and pathlessness are parallel symptoms.
structural_cues: 17:47 moves from listening to private framing and a hostile label; 17:48 moves from constructed comparisons to loss and inability to find a path.

activation_trace.role: Denied assent marks the present receptive failure.
Deferred time supplies the horizon across which reception will reverse.
Rousing what is still supplies the disputed transition into renewed agency.
Return after departure supplies continuity across the apparent ending.
Origination supplies the agentive basis for return.
The first beginning links future restoration back to initial production.
A directed call supplies the later speech event parallel to present recitation.
Answering speech supplies the response that is absent in the present encounter.

changed_reading.after: It marks a present interval of resistible address that will end in an unavoidable later call-and-response.
changed_reading.before: The veil is an indefinitely fixed separation from recited address.

context_deltas.mechanism: The denied later horizon is staged as fragmented matter, return by the first originator, and finally a call that receives an answer. The barrier is temporally asymmetric: recitation can be resisted now, but the later summons converts non-response into response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies present non-assent and a later call-answer sequence; I infer that the veil has a temporal limit and reversal, while an alternative is that the future sequence proves resurrection without describing the veil's duration.
structural_cues: 17:49 denies renewed creation, 17:51 answers with first origination and return, and 17:52 immediately pairs a future call with an answer.

activation_trace.role: Recited speech anchors the model in the focus event.
The shared middle interval supplies the site whose function can be contested.
A screening partition can buffer harmful passage as well as deny access.
Actual utterance supplies the human action capable of altering the interval.
Doing speech well supplies the relation-preserving alternative.
Incitement that corrupts relations supplies the opposing force operating in the interval.
The interhuman middle space locates where hidden agitation becomes social separation.

changed_reading.after: It may also preserve a volatile speech relation by spacing parties where hidden incitement would otherwise turn address into open hostility.
changed_reading.before: The barrier only excludes an audience from the reciter.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next speech instruction treats the relational interval as contested space: better speech can preserve relation, while incitement works inside the between-space to convert words into manifest enmity. The focus veil can therefore be carried as a protective buffer as well as an exclusion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies best speech versus incitement in the between-space; I infer a protective-buffer function for the focus veil, while the stronger alternative remains judicial exclusion of resistant hearers.
structural_cues: 17:53 orders better speech, then locates incitement between people, then names the enemy as manifest.

activation_trace.role: Blocked access anchors the filter whose scope is being expanded across media.
Covered operation allows the same hidden mechanism to persist under different evidence forms.
An overt mark supplies evidence designed to be perceptually available.
Attribution of falsehood supplies rejection despite the overt sign.
Visual perception makes the failed evidence channel explicitly non-auditory.
A vision supplies a second visual mode that becomes contested rather than decisive.
Testing converts displayed evidence into a discriminator of response.
Increase supplies the feedback by which warning magnifies the resistant response.

changed_reading.after: The same hidden resistance can metabolize heard, seen, and visionary evidence into further rejection, so changing modality does not remove the boundary.
changed_reading.before: The veil blocks a specifically auditory-recitative channel.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later visible signs and a shown vision do not bypass the focus barrier: the visible sign is denied, the vision becomes a test, and warning increases excess. The veil is thus a cross-modal response filter rather than a screen peculiar to recited sound.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed visual evidence and warning-driven increase; I infer one response filter across recitation, sign, and vision, while an alternative is that each episode has a separate historical cause.
structural_cues: 17:59 pairs an overt visual sign with denial; 17:60 makes a shown vision a test and closes with warning producing increased excess.

remaining_uncertainties: The relative weight of divine placement, hearer disposition, and protective buffering remains unresolved.
The protective reading of the relational interval in 17:53 is plausible but less direct than the exclusion and uptake models.
The concealment-inscription echo may be cadence rather than a mechanism intended by the sequence.
strongest_changes: The veil becomes an inverted reception mechanism in which varied recitation can increase recoil.
Repeated listening beside inward covering and auditory burden relocates concealment from audibility to uptake.
The resurrection sequence makes the boundary temporally asymmetric: resisted recitation now, answered summons later.
Failed visual signs and visions make the same resistance cross-modal rather than sound-specific.
summary.what_was_special: The tightest activation came from the sequence around 17:45: non-comprehension, inward covering, ear burden, actual listening, hostile redescribing, and path failure expose several layers of one hidden access problem. The 17:58 sound echo separately links concealment to inscription without collapsing their roots.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the concealed term whose sound is echoed.
Recitation makes the phonetic proximity experientially available.
Written composition supplies the textual domain into which the echo shifts.
An ordered written line supplies the near-sound counterpart to concealment.

changed_reading.after: Recited concealment is aurally shadowed by inscription, suggesting exploratorily that the hidden boundary is itself carried within the written order.
changed_reading.before: The concealed veil is simply opaque and outside disclosure.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Surprising because it turns on a near-homophonic cadence rather than shared-root identity; still valid because the focus modifier at word 12 is the direct anchor and 17:58 closes with a written-line root in the same position. Render only as a sonic-textual activation, never as lexical equivalence.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus closes with the modifier rooted in س ت ر, while 17:58 closes with a formally close modifier rooted in س ط ر.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Recitation can disclose a hidden interval by provoking non-assent.** `ق ر ء:B001/B002` gathers speech into recitation, `ب ي ن:B001/B002` separates and forms an interval, `ح ج ب:B001/B002` blocks with a veil, and `س ت ر:B001` conceals. A concealed veil is “made” precisely during reading; 17:41 has already shown message variation increasing recoil. I infer recitation does not create disbelief but renders its separating structure operative. The veil reads as relational incompatibility activated by encounter.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:82 clarifies that the veil is recipient-dependent differentiation: one descent becomes healing for trust and loss for misplacement, making separation an activated response.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Recitation activates a layered relational partition.** Lexical evidence: `ح ج ب B004` (inner partition) in `حِجَابًا`, and `س ت ر B001` (covering and concealment) in `مَّسْتُورًا`. Structural cue: doubled `بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ` locates the barrier relationally; 17:44 says praise is present but not understood, and 17:46 maps the partition inward as heart-covers and ear-weight. Assigned role: the inner partition blocks access, while concealment makes the blocking mechanism itself unavailable to those behind it. Abductive move: the packet supplies recitation followed by partition; I infer from the next ayah that failed reception, rather than absent sound, realizes the separation. Reading change: the veil is a layered epistemic boundary produced at the encounter with recitation, not merely a visible object placed in space.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:46 mapped the veil onto specific organs, confirming that the hidden partition of 17:45 is realized as a layered failure of hearing, integration, and bodily orientation.

words.gloss_range: opening conjunction that resumes the previous discourse and launches the conditional frame
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation, not reset. It carries the prior scene of human non-comprehension into the recitation condition, while its light fused onset with the temporal particle makes the conditional frame begin immediately.

topics.headline: connected opening to the recitation condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hidden barrier continues the previous problem of non-comprehension instead of starting a detached report.
topics.reason: The conjunction is compatible with coordination or resumption, and the CRITICAL rows tie that opening to the conditional scene and the prior discourse boundary.

topics.headline: brief fused onset into the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees a quick pickup into the condition, so the ayah feels joined while still entering a new temporal frame.
topics.reason: The particle is a proclitic before {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}), so the form and cadence rows add a local surface payoff without changing syntax.

words.gloss_range: temporal conditional particle making recitation a recurring trigger for the response
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the ayah a trigger-response structure. The perfect verb that follows is not a one-time past report; under this particle, recitation becomes the expected recurring condition for the answer clause. Its hamza-led entry also preserves a distinct conditional boundary after the opening connector.

topics.headline: certain recurring recitation trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the barrier is grammatically tied to each occurrence of recitation, not simply reported as a static past fact.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) as the temporal conditional governing the perfect protasis and pointing to the apodosis.

topics.headline: distinct particle entry inside the fused opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening connector does not swallow the conditional particle; the condition still enters as its own operator.
topics.reason: The form rows point to a real surface feature: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) remains independently legible after the prefixed connector.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect second-person singular recitation verb functioning as the addressed recurring trigger
words.prose: {{ar:قَرَأْتَ}} ({{tr:qara'ta}}) makes the addressed reciter the trigger-agent inside the condition. The local sense is recitation of the object that follows, while the root's gathering pressure makes that recitation feel like assembling the text into performed speech. The same phrase in (16:98) produces a different protective response, so this word helps mark recitation as a protection-switch here.
words.root_gloss_range: reciting and reading, with gathering or assembling pressure retained as root background under the local recitation sense

topics.headline: addressed reciter as condition-agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the barrier response begins from one addressed act of recitation, not from an abstract mention of scripture.
topics.reason: The verb is Form I perfect, second-person singular, and the conditional particle prevents a merely past-time reading.

topics.headline: recitation with gathering pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices recitation as constructive performed gathering of the Qur'an, while the local syntax still selects reciting rather than a separate act of collecting.
topics.reason: The object attachment to {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانَ}} ({{tr:al-qur'āna}}) selects recitation; root evidence allows gathering pressure as a qualifying lexical payoff.

topics.headline: same recitation formula, different protection response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase shared with (16:98) can trigger different protective actions: refuge-seeking there and divine barrier placement here.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete reference, and nothing in the local grammar blocks using it as a formula contrast.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative object: the known Qur'an as recited corpus completing the trigger phrase
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانَ}} ({{tr:al-qur'āna}}) completes the trigger as the definite object of the preceding recitation verb: not any reading, but the known recited corpus. The disputed collection or joining background survives as pressure, while the local verb strongly selects the recitation-root frame. The adjacent act-object echo defines the Qur'an through its mode of engagement, and the canonical hamza-bearing surface keeps that echo audibly interrupted. The next ayah (17:46) keeps the Qur'an-reception problem in view when divine making moves from an external barrier to coverings over hearts.
words.root_gloss_range: recitation, reading, and gathered corpus; joining or collection pressure is retained only as a narrowed derivational background

topics.headline: known corpus as direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition is tied to the known Qur'an as a recited object, not to generic reading or speech.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and accusative as the direct object of the preceding recitation verb.

topics.headline: recitation root with collection pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the Qur'an as recited speech and gathered corpus together, while the local phrase still favors the recitation derivation.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is meaningful but cannot replace the local root echo created by {{ar:قَرَأْتَ}} ({{tr:qara'ta}}).

topics.headline: act-object echo and hamza pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the act and object define each other, with the canonical hamza-bearing surface giving the phrase an interrupted texture.
topics.reason: The variant evidence clarifies sound pressure without changing the referent, and the immediate root repetition is local.

topics.headline: recited Qur'an leads into reception barriers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a two-ayah sequence: recitation produces an external barrier here, then Qur'an-understanding is blocked internally in (17:46).
topics.reason: The adjacent ayah reference is concrete and matches the local recitation and divine-placement frame.

words.gloss_range: divine first-person plural perfect of making, placing, or configuring a barrier in relation
words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:ja'alnā}}) is the hinge from human recitation to divine response. Its first-person plural perfect makes the barrier an enacted divine placement, and the syntax stretches that placing through the double between-frame before the object is named. Across the boundary, the divine referent described in (17:44) now speaks as the acting We. The same divine making continues in (17:46), where the obstruction moves inward to the faculties of reception.
words.root_gloss_range: making, rendering, appointing, and placing; local syntax selects relational placement/configuration rather than creation from nothing

topics.headline: divine We pivots from recitation to placement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah turn from the addressed reciter's act to divine agency at the center of the sentence.
topics.reason: The verb is first-person plural perfect and begins the apodosis after the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: placement, not creation from nothing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the barrier as something arranged into a relation between two sides, while broader making senses are limited by the local between-frame.
topics.reason: The local object and spatial complement license placing/configuring; ex-nihilo creation is not demanded by the grammar.

topics.headline: external barrier continues into internal covering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sequence from external separation in (17:45) to internal coverings in (17:46).
topics.reason: The adjacent repetition of divine making is concrete and supports the barrier sequence without overriding the local parse.

topics.headline: described He becomes speaking We
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse role shift: the divine referent moves from being described in (17:44) to speaking as the actor here.
topics.reason: The boundary rows give a coherent discourse payoff tied to the first-person plural verb.

words.gloss_range: passive participle adjective meaning hidden or covered, with possible concealing force by extension
words.prose: {{ar:مَّسْتُورًۭا}} ({{tr:mastūran}}) closes the ayah by making hiddenness the barrier's own quality. As an agreeing passive participle, it describes the barrier itself, not the reciter or the group; as a final word and marked passive-participle form, it leaves imperceptibility as the takeaway. The passive sense is primary, while the allowed concealing extension keeps the paradox alive: an unseen screen whose operation is screening. The root's curtain-covering image makes hiddenness feel like coveredness, the exposure contrasts in (18:90) and (41:22) sharpen the hidden-covering pole, and (17:46) moves that concealment into internal coverings. The final sound also fuses the adjective to the barrier phrase while the hidden/written echo with (17:58) and (33:6) remains only an echo, not a root replacement.
